To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we compute the entanglements entropy of a $(1 + 1)$-dimensionnal acoustic black hole in an atomic Bose-Einstein condensation; 2) we find a correction to the entropy that depends on the dispersion of the phonon field and is similar to the universal entropy of the XX spin chain; 3) the entropy is proportional to the size of the system measured in units of the healing length, as expected for a hydrodynamic system.

the entanglement of the Hawking radiation emitted by an acoustic black hole depends on the size and shape of the box in which it is trapped, in the same way as the entropy of a $(1 + 1)$-dimensionnal black hole.
we have calculated the entanglement spectrum of an acoustic black-hole in the presence of dispersion and found that it is similar to the entanglement of an XX Heisenberg spin chain.

the study of the entanglement of a Bose-Einstein gas with a black hole horizon in the near-hydrodynamic limit.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the acoustic black holes are not a good toy model for the study of the entanglement of quantum fields in the presence of a black hole horizon.
in both cases, the entanglement is not only a property of the horizon itself but also depends on the size and shape of the near-hydrodynamic region, as expected.
the entanglement of the Hawking radiation is the same as that of the ground state of the XX spin chain, but with a slightly different length scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the entanglement structure of the acoustic black hole is very similar to the one of a spin-1/ 2 Heisenberg chain.
the entropy of an acoustic black-hole in a Bose-Einsetin condensates can be computed using the entanglement properties of the XX chain.
the entropy of the acoustic black hole in the Bose-Einstein condensation is the same as that of a $(1 + 1)$-dimension gravitational black hole, but with a different universal correction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acoustic black hole in BECs can be used as a toy model to understand the universal corrections to the entanglement entropies of quantum field theories in one spatial dimension.
the entanglement properties of a $(1 + 1)$-dimension acoustic black hole are very similar to those of a gravitational $(1+ 1)$-black hole.
the acoustic black hole in the Bose-Einstein condensation provides a very simple toy model to test the universality of the entropy correction in the brick wall model.
